summary: Standing D-5 ground cabin in Oregon's Wallowa-Whitman National Forest, used for fire watch since 1916, re-roofed in 2021 and staffed in season.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest

access.note: Reached on foot by trail; the cab was locked up when a visitor arrived in September 2025. No source says whether visitors may enter the cab.

visit.trail_note: Backpacking route from the Buck Creek trailhead to a ridge trail that leads to the lookout, per a September 2025 trip report.

events.note: Selected as a fire detection site and staffed, with heliograph signaling, per NHLR. A 1916 newspaper item quoted by Oregon Lookouts places the heliograph on Granite Butte.
Current D-5 cab may date to as early as 1924 (NHLR); Oregon Lookouts states a ground cabin was constructed that year; firelookout.com gives 1924 with a question mark.
Fire on Buck Creek reported from the Mule Peak lookout station; no serious damage at the time.
Judy Wing named as lookout personnel for several years in the 1980s (firelookout.com).
Two employees evacuated by helicopter as flames threatened; firefighters wrapped the building in fire-resistant material; an aircraft dropped retardant.
A Forest Service worker was evacuated from the lookout by helicopter during a fast-moving wildfire, as quoted from the Baker City Herald.
New cedar shake roof and paint.
Attendant on site for a few days early in the season; the lookout was locked up when the trip report writers arrived.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 8,395 ft (2,559 m) matches the brief's record and is kept. firelookout.com (8,679 ft) and the 2025 trip report (8,554 ft) differ and are not used for the record.
The register hedges with 'may have been constructed as early as 1924'; the Oregon Lookouts history states 1924 without hedging. The record keeps 1924 as an approximate date.

notes_for_editor: Built year is approximate (NHLR says as early as 1924; firelookout.com has a question mark). The 1916 heliograph placement conflicts: NHLR ties it to Mule Peak, the 1916 newspaper item quoted by Oregon Lookouts places it on Granite Butte; both kept, unresolved. Staffing and today's status rest on one 2025 blog trip report and a 1980s name from firelookout.com; no Forest Service document found. Access 'restricted' is an inference from the locked cab and staffing; no official visitor policy found. Judy Wing is named only as a historical lookout attendant. One websearch used. Cheryl Hill's standing-lookouts list marks Mule Peak unmanned, which conflicts with the 2025 trip report; both are reported. Record access 'unknown' and staffing 'unknown' could be updated from the sources above.
